answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may claim work or vote. The protocol caps each account’s influence by its locked stake, so creating a thousand identities does not multiply the attacker’s weight; splitting the same deposit only divides it. A river of fake profiles still has to fund every claim, while the lockup ties up capital and exposes it to slashing if fraud is proven. Neither a nebula nor a sonnet can make that stake free.
